page: Amazon Web Services u-18tb1.112xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8280L processors. It features 448 vCPUs across 224 physical cores running at 2.7 GHz, utilizing the Nitro hypervisor. The system is equipped with 18,432 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, providing approximately 41.14 GB of memory per physical core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, but features a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-core CPU capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 403,244.15 and a PassMark CPU score of 114,402.45. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 22,379.25 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 514.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Redis SET operations perform at a top-tier rate of 320.83 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is relatively modest, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,010.0 and an average stress-ng single-core score of 1,556.08. Additionally, the PassMark memory score is in the bottom 10% at 1,132.78, indicating potential latency or architectural overheads in massive multi-socket memory configurations.

From a cost efficiency perspective, this server represents a highly specialized, high-density hardware class designed for massive in-memory workloads. The absence of bundled local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is supported by the 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The extreme memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it a premium resource, meaning it is inefficient for workloads that do not actively utilize the 18 TB memory footprint.

The u-18tb1.112xlarge is designed for massive in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise resource planning systems like SAP HANA, and memory-intensive data warehousing. It is also suitable for high-throughput redis caching layers and large-scale static web serving.
